sentences.cn_text: 人们常常抱怨塑料过于耐用。
sentences.en_text: People often complain that plastics are too durable.

sentences.cn_text: 从珠穆朗玛峰到马里亚纳海沟，水瓶、购物袋和其他垃圾遍布地球各处，因为塑料无处不在且难以分解。
sentences.en_text: Water bottles, shopping bags, and other trash litter the planet, from Mount Everest to the Mariana Trench, because plastics are everywhere and don’t break down easily.

sentences.cn_text: 但有些塑料材料会随时间发生变化。
sentences.en_text: But some plastic materials change over time.

sentences.cn_text: 它们会开裂、卷曲。
sentences.en_text: They crack and frizzle.

sentences.cn_text: 它们会「渗出」添加剂。
sentences.en_text: They “weep” out additives.

sentences.cn_text: 它们会融化成泥状物。
sentences.en_text: They melt into sludge.

sentences.cn_text: 所有这些都给试图保存重要文化物品的机构（如博物馆）带来了巨大难题。
sentences.en_text: All of which creates huge headaches for institutions, such as museums, trying to preserve culturally important objects.

sentences.cn_text: 面临风险的塑料物品种类繁多，令人眼花缭乱：早期收音机、前卫雕塑、迪士尼电影的赛璐珞动画静帧、第一颗人造心脏。
sentences.en_text: The variety of plastic objects at risk is dizzying: early radios, avant-garde sculptures, celluloid animation stills from Disney films, the first artificial heart.

sentences.cn_text: 某些文物尤其脆弱，因为一些塑料艺术先驱并不总是知道如何正确配制成分，聚合物化学家西娅·范奥斯滕说道，她在几年前退休前曾在荷兰文化遗产局工作数十年。
sentences.en_text: Certain artifacts are especially vulnerable because some pioneers in plastic art didn’t always know how to mix ingredients properly, says Thea van Oosten, a polymer chemist who, until retiring a few years ago, worked for decades at the Cultural Heritage Agency of the Netherlands.

sentences.cn_text: 「这就像烤蛋糕：如果没有准确的配比，就会失败。」她说。
sentences.en_text: “It’s like baking a cake: If you don’t have exact amounts, it goes wrong.” she says.

sentences.cn_text: 「你制作的物品本身就已经是一颗定时炸弹。」
sentences.en_text: “The object you make is already a time bomb.”

sentences.cn_text: 而有时，这并非艺术家的过错。
sentences.en_text: And sometimes, it’s not the artist’s fault.

sentences.cn_text: 20世纪60年代，意大利艺术家皮耶罗·吉拉尔迪开始创作数百件鲜艳多彩的泡沫作品。
sentences.en_text: In the 1960s, the Italian artist Piero Gilardi began to create hundreds of bright, colorful foam pieces.

sentences.cn_text: 这些作品包括小型玫瑰花床等物件，以及数十件「自然地毯」——用泡沫南瓜、卷心菜和西瓜装饰的大型矩形作品。
sentences.en_text: Those pieces included small beds of roses and other items as well as a few dozen “nature carpets” — large rectangles decorated with foam pumpkins, cabbages, and watermelons.

sentences.cn_text: 他希望观众能在地毯上走动——这意味着它们必须足够耐用。
sentences.en_text: He wanted viewers to walk around on the carpets — which meant they had to be durable.

sentences.cn_text: 不幸的是，他所使用的聚氨酯泡沫本质上并不稳定。
sentences.en_text: Unfortunately, the polyurethane foam he used is inherently unstable.

sentences.cn_text: 它特别容易受光损害，到20世纪90年代中期，吉拉尔迪的南瓜、玫瑰和其他造型开始开裂并破碎。
sentences.en_text: It’s especially vulnerable to light damage, and by the mid-1990s, Gilardi’s pumpkins, roses, and other figures were splitting and crumbling.

sentences.cn_text: 博物馆将其中一些作品锁存在暗处。
sentences.en_text: Museums locked some of them away in the dark.

sentences.cn_text: 于是范奥斯滕和同事们着手保护吉拉尔迪的雕塑。
sentences.en_text: So van Oosten and her colleagues worked to preserve Gilardi’s sculptures.

sentences.cn_text: 他们为部分作品注入了稳定剂和固化剂。
sentences.en_text: They infused some with stabilizing and consolidating chemicals.

sentences.cn_text: 范奥斯滕将这些化学物质称为「防晒剂」，因为其目的是防止进一步的光损害并修复受损的聚合物纤维。
sentences.en_text: Van Oosten calls those chemicals “sunscreens” because their goal was to prevent further light damage and rebuild worn polymer fibers.

sentences.cn_text: 她感到自豪的是，数件雕塑甚至再次得以展出，尽管有时需要放置在保护罩下。
sentences.en_text: She is proud that several sculptures have even gone on display again, albeit sometimes beneath protective cases.

sentences.cn_text: 尽管有范奥斯滕这样的成功案例，塑料保存工作很可能会变得更加困难。
sentences.en_text: Despite success stories like van Oosten’s, preservation of plastics will likely get harder.

sentences.cn_text: 旧物品持续退化。
sentences.en_text: Old objects continue to deteriorate.

sentences.cn_text: 更糟的是，专为分解而设计的可生物降解塑料正变得越来越普遍。
sentences.en_text: Worse, biodegradable plastics designed to disintegrate, are increasingly common.

sentences.cn_text: 而这里所关乎的不仅仅是单个物品。
sentences.en_text: And more is at stake here than individual objects.

sentences.cn_text: 新里斯本科技大学保护与修复助理教授乔安娜·利亚·费雷拉指出，考古学家是在博物馆研究文物之后，才首次界定了人类历史上的重要材料时代——石器时代、铁器时代等等。
sentences.en_text: Joana Lia Ferreira, an assistant professor of conservation and restoration at the NOVA School of Science and Technology, notes that archaeologists first defined the great material ages of human history — Stone Age, Iron Age, and so on — after examining artifacts in museums.

sentences.cn_text: 我们如今生活在塑料时代，她说，「我们今天决定收藏什么、决定保存什么……将对未来人们如何看待我们产生重大影响。」
sentences.en_text: We now live in an age of plastic, she says, “and what we decide to collect today, what we decide to preserve...will have a strong impact on how in the future we’ll be seen.”
